title: Serious Harm from Pressure Bandage Immobilisation Applied to an Envenomed Snakebite Patient; A Case Report
content: Although pressure bandage immobilisation (PBI) stopped systemic venom absorption in animal experiments, the real-world utility of PBI for snake bites in humans is incompletely defined. PBI is often applied for extended periods in rural Australia where snake bites are common. We describe a case of a man with taipan envenomation who required an above knee amputation after 12 hours of PBI. We hypothesise that this was the result of overzealous PBI application leading to a compartment syndrome and tissue ischaemia. The potential harms of PBI necessitate further research to define the incremental advantage of PBI in snakebites over immobilisation alone.
